speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and an imbalance. To help me determine the cause, can you describe if your dizziness feels like the room is spinning or if it is more of a feeling of lightheadedness?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the constant spinning sensation suggests a vestibular issue. You mentioned increased garlic intake and a recent cold—can you tell me if this dizziness is triggered by specific head movements or if it occurs even when you are lying still?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) is unlikely due to the sustained nature; the most probable diagnosis is Vestibular Neuritis or Labyrinthitis given the acute onset of constant vertigo following a viral illness (recent cold), though early Meniere's disease remains a differential to rule out.
